description.narrative:
Agriculture remains the backbone of the Tanzanian economy and its vision for the future. About 75% of Tanzanians depend on agriculture for their livelihoods, while 85% of the country’s poor live in rural areas and rely on subsistence agriculture as their primary source of income. Whitin agriculture, the horticulture sector has been the fastest growing sub-sector over the past years. Horticultural produce has always been a part of Tanzania’s diet and mainstay of many Tanzanians. In addition, horticulture presents high rates of women and smallholding farmer inclusiveness, labor absorption and high technology adoption. The Southern Highlands of Tanzania presents many advantages for farming high-value horticulture crops (favorable weather, fertile lands, rivers for irrigation, availability of labor, strategic location for exports), but the value chain is not set up in an organised industry, with lack of technical knowledge and infrastructure.
The East-Africa, Tanzania: a Farmers’ Roadmap of Expanding Successful Horticulture (EAT - FRESH) is a consortium program led by TechForce whose purpose is to Improve the performance of the horticulture sector in the Southern Highlands and to make the Iringa and Njombe regions viable sources for premium horticulture produce by investing in agri-logistics, sustainable fertilizer production, and in smallholder farmer development, enabling inclusive business development, and improving stakeholders’ socio-economic conditions, all through solid collaboration between farmers, industry and government.
As part of the consortium Agriterra will support horticultural farmers organisations of high value vegetables such as French beans, snow peas and avocado through capacity building in horticultural skills, governance and entrepreneurship. Under the consortium, Agriterra will be responsible for:
Activities
- 50 farmer organisations scoped
- 15 farmer organisations assessed
- 23 trainings delivered (6 MyCoop, 6 record keeping, 2 financial management, 2 youth kick-off, 2 female leadership, 2 supervisory board, 2 ToT on vegetable production)
- 15 farmer organisations which receive services from Agriterra

Outputs
- 2,240 people trained
Results
- Youth & women councils set up
- Commercial contracts reached
- Mobilised loans agreed
- Increase in women and youth board participation
- Creation of jobs at farmer organisation level
